<description>
This is a simple mempool PR that fixes #33510.

Evicting mempool transactions by age (`-mempoolexpiry`, default two weeks) is
incentive-incompatible: it may drop transactions that could still be mined
As discussed IRL and in #33510, this PR hence removes age-based eviction entirely.

Transactions now leave the mempool only via size limiting (`-maxmempool`),
replacement, conflicts, or inclusion in a block. The `EXPIRY` removal reason is
dropped. `-mempoolexpiry` is retained as a hidden no-op that warns when set, so
existing configurations keep starting.

Nice side effects:
- With expiry gone, the `entry_time` index has no readers. Removing it saves an
  ordered-tree node per mempool entry and drops a now unused Boost
  include.
- The `DynamicMemoryUsage()` per-entry estimate drops from three indexes to
  two, so within the same `-maxmempool` budget the mempool fits slightly more
  transactions.
</description>

[2026-11-03] c:6605091861 comment by ismaelsadeeq (member):
Thanks for review @ajtowns @stickies-v @maflcko @tumutech @fametrano @musaHaruna

I addressed most feedback and concerns in the latest push or with reply below.

[quoted text omitted]
The best thing to do in this case is to update the node, because expiry doesn't help here either. The transactions can just be rebroadcast again, and as you mentioned, this cycle can go on forever, so I don't think this is a valid reason to keep expiry.

[quoted text omitted]
I think the fact that it is possible, and that we see such transactions mined, should suffice. We assume miners act rationally and follow incentive compatibility for inclusion, so whatever they mine is economically incentive compatible at that moment in time.

[quoted text omitted]
There is a legitimate concern raised by @mzumsande, and offline by a few other people, that this approach also aids censorship, so I won't be comfortable shipping it.

[quoted text omitted]
I thought about this, and that's why the default never uses the mempool to raise the fee rate estimate, so it's not going to be a problem at all. It may only affect users who explicitly request the mempool estimator alone, and I assume those are advanced users who know what they're getting into and should have a sentinel max, e.g. an LND budget sweeper.

[quoted text omitted]
I feel strongly about this. I think the reasons mentioned above by you and @ajtowns are thin. We should not incentivize free relay, the expiry use case is a bit speculative, and @0xB10C's data already showed that most of the expired txs eventually get mined. In the adversarial scenario expiry won't help either, since the attacker can just keep cycling it. The fee rate estimator is not affected. So it would be more ideal to just clean this code up and remove this feature, it is unnecessary.

Also, if we decide to remove wallet rebroadcast and only rebroadcast what's not in the mempool, we would still have a privacy leak if users expire, because we'd expire our own txs and then rebroadcast them again. The same thing happens on reload: loading mempool.dat drops entries older than the expiry, so after a restart the node treats its own aged txs as missing and rebroadcasts them.
